title: Tiered Upsell Playbook — Tech Economics + Deployment Readiness
body:
Purpose:
A lightweight, operational playbook to run technically-led expansion conversations where the buyer’s primary levers are performance, isolation, and contractual SLAs (Dedicated capacity, Private deployment, premium SLA add-ons). This is a working doc — focused on signals, technical readiness gating, quick ROI checks, and an outreach/cadence + handoff checklist for SEs and CSMs.

When to use this playbook (quick signals):
- Customer consistently hitting >70% of current dedicated pool or sustained high burst activity (p95 throughput)
- Repeated requests for hardware isolation, region-specific residency, or contractual uptime guarantees
- Security/compliance asks that cannot be satisfied on hosted plans (KMS/HSM, VPC peering, on-prem installs)
- Performance regressions traced to noisy neighbors or multi-tenant variability
- QBR notes: customer mentions roadmap items tied to latency-sensitive features (real-time chat, streaming inferencing)

High-level play flow (short):
1) Trigger + qualify (CSM identifies signal, opens expansion ticket, schedule discovery)
2) Technical discovery (SE deep dive; capture benchmarks + integration constraints)
3) Internal gating (SRE/Infra + pricing ops review feasibility and estimate)
4) Proposal (cost / ROI scenarios + SLA terms draft)
5) Pilot/PoC or canary migration (if Private or Dedicated migration needed)
6) Close and onboarding + success plan (capacity runbook, rollback, monitoring)

Discovery checklist (SE + CSM joint):
- Current plan and exact limits (concurrency, qps, tokens/day)
- Typical request shape: avg length, worst-case length, streaming vs batch
- Peak vs baseline traffic times and p95 latency targets
- KV-cache/prefix reuse patterns (are requests highly cacheable?)
- Existing observability hooks: can we ingest traces? Do they have example logs / histograms?
- Data residency / compliance constraints (region, data exfiltration concerns)
- Integrations required: VPC peering, private endpoints, SSO/KMS, on-prem network topology
- Driver install / runtime constraints (CUDA/driver versions, custom kernels)
- SLA must-haves: RTO/RPO, maintenance windows, extended support hours
- Stakeholders: engineering, infra/security, procurement, legal (name + contact)

Minimum Technical Readiness (gating criteria to propose Dedicated / Private):
- Workload reproducible in our infra: customer provides 3 representative requests + load profile
- Performance delta threshold: Dedicated variant should improve p95 latency by >=20% or reduce per-token cost by >=15% (if cost is the ask)
- Clear data boundary requirements documented and agreed (where logs/inputs stored)
- Security review passes basic checklist: SSO + SCIM, KMS integration capabilities confirmed, network CIDRs for peering
- Support SLA level identified (S1/S2 escalation contacts, 24x7 or business hours)

Quick ROI sketch (to capture in QBR or proposal slide):
- Current monthly token spend: $X (hosted)
- Estimated monthly cost on Dedicated (baseline pool + burst): $Y
- Migration/one-time engineering cost (estimate): $Z
- Net monthly delta: Y - X (sign indicates save or increase)
- Payback horizon: Z / abs(Y - X) months
- Qualitative benefits: predictable latency, isolation, compliance satisfaction (list items)

Template: ROI line (fill in during discovery)
- avg_tokens_per_month, avg_qps, avg_seq_len, current_cost_per_token, dedicated_unit_cost_estimate, migration_hours_estimate, se_hours, expected_savings_pct

Example objection handling (short bullets):
- "We’re fine on hosted" -> ask for 30-day active capacity graph; highlight p95 spikes and a concrete SLA commitment; offer a short canary at no additional charge for first 30 days to demonstrate stability.
- "Private is too slow to set up" -> show standard 45-day on-prem timeline with parallel tasks; propose interim Dedicated pool while Private is provisioned.
- "We can’t justify price" -> walk through payback horizon and business risk reduction (SLA credits, compliance avoidance, reduced incident MTTR). Present flexible pricing: commit tiers, trial credits, or seasonal bursts.

Negotiable pricing levers (for SE+CSM to discuss internally):
- Commit term length (6/12/24) with progressive discounts
- Baseline capacity vs burst pools (baseline reserved cheaper, burst at premium)
- Support tier: business hours vs 24x7 with on-call engineering (price uplift)
- Data retention/observability add-ons (longer metric retention -> extra fee)

QBR slide checklist (what to prepare for an expansion conversation):
- Usage summary + trending (tokens, requests, p50/p95 latencies)
- Cost breakdown (current hosted spend by model and route)
- Incident log + root-cause notes for last 90 days (if capacity related)
- Proposed capacity / config for Dedicated or Private (est. throughput)
- ROI summary slide (numbers + assumptions)
- Migration/PoC plan with timeline and owners

Outreach cadence (example):
- Day 0: CSM intro email with 1-sentence value prop + ask for discovery slot (include 3 metrics we saw)
- Day 3: Follow-up Slack/LinkedIn if no reply. Mention limited pilot slots.
- Day 7: SE-led discovery meeting (30–60m) with checklist pre-filled; capture artifacts.
- Day 10: Internal readiness sync (CS + SE + pricing + SRE)
- Day 14: Proposal draft to customer, optional signing of MOU for pilot

Handoff checklist to Solutions Engineering / Professional Services:
- Access: API keys, sample payloads, traces, dev/staging environment credentials
- Data agreements executed (if Private/on-prem)
- Target performance metrics and SLA wording agreed
- Test plan: latency tests, throughput ramps, failure/fallback tests
- Rollback plan and cutover window

Renewal tracker row template (use in tracker sheet):
- Customer short name, account owner, current tier, committed qps/tokens, pilot requested (Y/N), proposed new tier, est_monthly_cost, migration_estimate_hours, legal_stage, target_close_date, next_meeting_owner

Playbook scripts (short, usable in emails/Slack):
- CSM intro email: "Quick note — since X we’ve seen sustained peak traffic that looks like it could benefit from reserved capacity. Can we schedule 30m to review a 2-scenario ROI I sketched? No obligation; I think you’ll find the latency delta interesting. — Aisha"
- SE follow-up (post discovery): "Thanks for the session. Attached are the three benchmark runs we talked about. Next step: internal sizing review with infra and pricing. Are you able to approve a 2-week pilot window?"

Risk table (short):
- Migration complexity -> mitigate with canary + rollback + dry-run
- Legal/Procurement delay -> mitigate with MOU + exec sponsor involvement
- Performance not as expected -> include objective benchmark gates in pilot contract and shared acceptance criteria

Open items / notes to self:
- Build a simple calculator in the tracker sheet to auto-populate ROI numbers from usage export (todo for growth-ops).
- Ask pricing ops for fixed templates for 6/12/24 month commits to speed approvals (JIRA-4132).
- Validate Private deployment standard lead time with infra team: current target 45 days (confirm Feb SLA runbook).

Next steps (immediate play actions when signal detected):
1) CSM creates tracker row and notifies #cs-upsell with short summary + links to traces.
2) Book SE discovery within 7 days.
3) Internal readiness review by day 10.
4) Draft proposal by day 14; offer pilot/MOU option.

Appendix: quick references
- Slack: #cs-upsell, #se-uptakes
- Confluence: /CS/upsell-framework -> intake form, pricing bands, legal templates
- Suggested slide deck: solutions-templates/upsell-dedicated-pitch-v2 (internal repo)

End notes: keep this doc short and iterative. This is a pragmatic, technically oriented script for upsells where latency/isolation/SLA are the differentiators. Please add case examples here when you run pilots (marker: add customer name + outcome).
